correctness.rationale: Independence of the central lines gives coordinatewise alternating determinants, also in characteristic two. The first closed-neighborhood subspace is the direct sum of a line in each nonzero coordinate and the full plane in each zero coordinate. Its dimension is at least t, but it is proper, so it strictly enlarges the starting line for t≥2. It contains nonzero vectors supported in two different coordinate planes. Their commuting subspaces together span the quotient, so the next iterate is full, proving uniform height two and, by monotonicity, that only zero and the full space are fixed. A dependent coordinate pair has a common nonzero commuting vector there; if it equals an endpoint the endpoints already commute. For coordinatewise independent pairs no nonzero common perpendicular exists, but the two chosen projections in different factors give a three-edge path. Such pairs exist in every field. Counting an ordered basis independently in each plane gives the stated ordered quotient-vector count. For t=1 the components really are the nonzero parts of lines. Read RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md and check_rcg.py; reported finite calculations are supplementary, not an all-field proof, and the uploaded script was not rerun.

value.rationale: The useful feature is an exact separation between the graph metric and the linear-neighborhood iteration on a natural direct-sum family. It identifies which pairs need a third step even when every nonzero starting line already spans the quotient after two iterations, and classifies the closed subspaces in all characteristics. The pair census makes the distinction quantitative over finite fields. The prior diameter-three example, by itself, is not the asserted value.
